notes.nneebaka: Je dors (I sleep) or je me couche (I go to bed).
notes.ekyenkya: Prendre le petit-déjeuner: to have breakfast.
notes.akola: Il travaille; elle travaille for a woman.
notes.tukola: Nous travaillons. In speech, people often say on travaille.
notes.ndaba: Regarder la télé: to watch TV.
notes.osha: Faire la vaisselle: to wash the dishes.

guidebook.intro: Describe your day from waking up to going to bed. Many daily actions in French are reflexive: you wake yourself, you put yourself to bed.

tips.title: Je me réveille, je me lève
body: Verbs for what you do to yourself take **me** (myself), **te** (yourself), **se** (him/herself): **Je me réveille** (I wake up), **Je me lève** (I get up), **Je me couche** (I go to bed). Before a vowel: **Je m’habille** (I get dressed).
In the dictionary, they’re listed with **se**: **se réveiller, se lever, se coucher**.

tips.title: Je travaille, nous travaillons
body: Most verbs end in **-er** and follow one pattern. For **travailler** (to work): **je travaille, tu travailles, il travaille, nous travaillons, vous travaillez, ils travaillent**.
The endings **-e, -es, -e, -ent** all sound the same, so **il travaille** and **ils travaillent** sound identical. Only **nous** and **vous** sound different.

tips.title: J’aime jouer
body: After **aimer** (to like), put the verb as it is in the dictionary: **J’aime jouer au foot. J’aime lire.** With a noun, French uses **le, la, les**: **J’aime la musique**.

culture.title: Meals
body: **Le petit-déjeuner** (breakfast), **le déjeuner** (lunch) and **le dîner** (dinner). In Belgium, Switzerland and parts of Africa, people say **le déjeuner** for breakfast and **le dîner** for lunch, and the evening meal is **le souper**.
